_comment: Known-failing backend tests. A ratchet: entries may be removed, never added without a deliberate decision. See check_backend_tests.py. 2026-09-04: removed the edge blocked-path websocket test from this list. It was not a code defect -- it asserted that '/tools' is on the edge blocklist, which it is not and shows no sign of ever having been. The test now derives the prefix from _BLOCKED_PREFIXES, so it tests the property rather than a memorised list, and it passes. 19 -> 18. Also removed the three TestB5TheGpuNoteIsTrue entries: not code defects either. They read shared/knowledge/<id>.md and shared/knowledge/MEMORY.md, and the knowledge layer became scope-partitioned (<scope>/<kind>/<id>.md) underneath them, so all three failed with FileNotFoundError/StopIteration against a note that was present the whole time. They find the note by id now and skip when this instance has none. 18 -> 15. 2026-09-05: removed the runner-brake and semantic-index entries. Both pass alone and in two consecutive full-suite runs, so they are fixed rather than known-failing. 11 -> 9. Nothing was ADDED: the nine failures reported against this file on 2026-09-05 were all repaired at their source instead. Seven in test_worktree_isolation_end_to_end.py were suite-order pollution -- the `ctx` fixtures in test_chat_provider_containment.py and test_development_chat_scope.py called importlib.reload(chat_context), which rebinds that module's CLASSES while every already-imported test module keeps the old ones, so is_build_provider's isinstance answered False for a provider subclassed at collection time. The other two were real regressions in the tests themselves: a rewritten structural assertion that never matched the tree it was written against, and a fake whose signature had drifted from the function it stood in for.
